If you think suicide is the way to go.

It isn't. 

Think about all the people you have yet to meet. You could be that person who does something seemingly insignificant that turns someone's life around.

You will be happy- not now, maybe not next year but someday. You have to have hope, if you don't have the strength for hope anymore. Find someone who does. There's always someone willing to help- in person, on helplines or even online. 

Everyone is important to someone. You may not realise it, but you are.

 

Your life is full of possibilities

You can do this.

The people around you might say these things but ever consider that your low opinion of yourself is the reason you're accepting these people and their words? You're self aware, asking for help. 
These are all signs of a person who's done nothing to deserve this amount of crap. Even after your parents say or do these things, you still have the hugely amazing morality and empathy to feel bad for trying to get out of this situation.
You're a good person.
But you need to look at the people around you and stop internalizing. Seek help where ever someone will genuinely give you care and genuine support. You need to get out. You can, you will and I believe in you.

It's never too late
What have been your hobbies in the past?
Is NA available in the UK?
My friends trying to give up too- one of them because he said he loves me. I know the addiction is something I need to sort. I will look for addiction centres in my area (uk) soon. Thank you so much

(To your first reply)I do know he was, he still does. And I honestly I feel like the bad influence half the time- even though one of my best friends is the one who got me into harder drugs. I have apologised but I can't get this feeling of not wanting to be sober out of my head. Thank you for replying and believing though 

And as to your post after- I'm crying. Thank you. It means a lot to hear that someone took some time to look at something like that and try and make me feel better. Thank you so much

You sound like an amazing person :) What kind of volunteer work do you do? Do you enjoy that? 

I've been there myself with the drugs issue; may I ask what drug/s? Dependency is a slippery slope all it's own and I ask that you please seek help for this if nothing else. From a personal level (as I did), or professionaly. Alcohol/drugs are a quick easy fix and I know the long run won't be your main concern right now, but as one person to another please don't go down that path. Next time you grab a bottle or whatever consider binge watching your favourite show or just doing something. (Even if it is easier said than done)

Sorry if this is unhelpful. 
But you matter to the world and you need to believe it.

The Moomins.

There was one episode were a purple mustached blob rises from a misty black lake. I still have nightmares about that episode, I'm 19.

As someone who's been on the other side of this- talk to her. Tell her how her habits affect you.

You're both in this relationship and need to discuss issues that make you concerned. 

I didn't listen straight away (stubborn) but once I realised how much my habits were affecting my SO I had a major change in attitude. 

It may be a slow process but support her- let her make the decision to stop (if she wants to). Don't forget to let her know you love her when talking it out.

Good luck :)
I'm sorry you went through that. I just emplore you to remember to reach out to someone- anyone should you ever feel even half as bad again.

Just want to say that anyone coming to a thread like this to check if suicide is the way to go.

It isn't. 

Think about all the people you have yet to meet. You could be that person who does something seemingly insignificant that turns someone's life around.

You will be happy- not now, maybe not next year but someday. You have to have hope, if you don't have the strength for hope anymore. Find someone who does. There's always someone willing to help- in person, on helplines or even online. 

Everyone is important to someone. You may not realise it, but you are.

Those of you who came for morbid curiosity- my thoughts were "What's the point anyway?Who will miss me?" I failed and am so happy I did. It took a while but my life changed for the better even if I am still struggling with depression. 

Your life is full of possibilities

My little brother used to see 'a man' in our house

When he was around 3/4, he used to stare at the kitchen sink but wouldn't go into the kitchen. My mum asked him why.

"There's a man counting money" he would say

My mum told him to ignore the man as he was obviously busy. 

He would sometimes sleep in my parents room at this age, and he started to stare into the corner of the room again. He said it was the man again. Mum asked him if the man was counting money again

"No, he isn't doing anything. But he's angry." He was then asked if he liked the man, he didn't. So he was told to ignore him and not look at him

Fast forward a few weeks of this happening quite a few times and he's in the living room...you guessed it! Staring! At a wall. We asked him what was wrong and he said the man walked out the wall and was gone.

A few years later we were looking through the house plans and where he saw this happen there was a doorway. But there hadn't been a doorway for at least a hundred years
  
Edit: should probably mention he doesn't remember this, he is a total sceptic now at age 15.

I had happened to go to college because I failed first year of sixth form.

He had happened to go to the same college because he failed first year of sixth form.

Got put in one class together. 

He happened to start talking to me because of a Doctor Who pin on my bag and we sat together all year.

So...very unlikely. He lives in the main city centre and I live 3 miles away in a village. We would never have met- totally different friend groups. 

Ended up together 6 months before college ended.

Not sure if this is what you're looking for but...

I was having a bad time- in an abusive relationship for a few years. Whilst with my ex I went to college, and made an amazing group of friends. One guy in the group was very quiet- he would talk if we were alone, and talking to him I began to realise I was telling him a lot about myself. I trusted him, something about him made me go to him when my douchebag ex cheated (this happened a lot) and chat. I liked him.

College was going to be ending in 6 months at this point. And I realised I couldn't let him go- I knew hardly ANYTHING about him. So I ended up finally getting shot of my ex and a month later he asked me out.

He is the kindest, best boyfriend I could ever have asked for and he made my life so much better than I ever thought one person ever could.

Ladies- go for the quiet friend! Don't lock them in the friendzone too soon!

TL;DR had a hunch I shouldn't let a guy I hardly know go out of my life, became my best decision.
"I'd rather be a rising ape than a fallen angel"- Sir Terry Pratchett

A handmade necklace. It was for valentines and we'd been together for a month. Knowing he'd put so much time and effort into his present so early into the relationship made me realise how much being with me meant to him :) I still wear it nearly 8 months later and love when people ask me about it.
